findings.title: website_name bypasses TL0 website hiding
findings.body: include_website_name is missing the trailing ? that ActiveModel Serializers requires (every other include hook in this file is include_*?). The hook is therefore never called, so website_name is always serialized. The method also reads user_profile.website directly and is not listed in untrusted_attributes, which is what hides website from anonymous viewers of TL0 users. Those viewers now receive the website host and, when the domain heuristic matches, the path, defeating the spam/privacy restriction. The serializer spec's untrusted_attributes list was not updated, so this leak is untested.

findings.title: Invalid or non-ASCII websites disappear from the profile
findings.body: website_name parses the stored website with URI and rescues every error to nil, then returns nil when host is nil. The profile template now renders the globe link only when model.website_name is present, replacing the old client split that displayed the host segment of any non-empty URL. Ruby's URI rejects non-ASCII hosts (IDN) and many user-typed URLs, so those profiles lose the website label entirely instead of falling back to the hostname. The second URI() call that appends the path is outside the rescue, so a parse failure there raises during serialization.

findings.title: Domain check treats unrelated hosts as the same site
findings.body: The else branch treats the website as the same site whenever Discourse.current_hostname ends with '.' plus the website host, and the elsif branch equates any two hosts that share every label after the first when they have the same label count greater than 2. That matches public suffixes and unrelated names, not just the instance domain: a site at forum.example.com will expand http://com/login to 'com/login', and http://evil.example.com/phish will be expanded the same way as a real sibling such as www. Host comparison is also case-sensitive against Discourse.current_hostname while URI#host is lowercased, so Example.com vs example.com skips the equal-host branch and omits the path the feature is supposed to show.
